evidence: paper: \int_0^T a\,\nabla\pi\,dt = \Delta \int_0^T a w\,dt + \int_0^T a' w\,dt - \operatorname{div}\int_0^T a g\,dt.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean states the identity tested against a compact smooth real ψ and componentwise in k, which is the meaning of the paper's display as an identity of distributions. Term by term: ⟨Δ∫aw, ψ⟩ = ∫ (∫aw) Δψ is the first Lean term (scalarLaplacian ψ); ⟨∫a'w, ψ⟩ is the second (deriv a); ⟨-div ∫ag, ψ⟩ = +∑_i ∫ (∫a g_{ki}) ∂_i ψ is the third, so the paper's minus sign on the divergence becomes the Lean's plus sign on the integrated-by-parts term. The time integral over Icc 0 T equals the paper's ∫_0^T, and the hypotheses on a match C_c^∞(0,T) exactly (smooth, tsupport ⊆ Ioo 0 T). The sign convention w_Lean = u - v = -w, pi_Lean = -pi, g_Lean = -g applies to every term of this identity, which is homogeneous of degree one in (w, pi, g). The paper's accompanying assertion that the three right-hand terms lie in H^{-2}, L^2 and H^{-3} is not part of these statements; the corresponding quantitative control in Lean is PressureFunctionals.averagedPressureDifferenceValue_bound against the H^3 test norm, which I did not compare clause by clause.
